root_cause: The public website tried to become bilingual by translating the already-rendered Dutch DOM at runtime. This made language switching dependent on client-side events, mutation timing, browser state and a remote AI request. The result repeatedly allowed English to appear selected while the actual document remained Dutch.
prevention: Public website language variants must be built as deterministic locale routes under /nl and /en.
Language switching navigates to the corresponding locale URL instead of mutating the full static document in place.
Each localized document must carry the correct html lang value, canonical URL and reciprocal hreflang links including x-default.
Internal website links must remain within the active locale.
Production English route generation fails closed when any static translation is unresolved; mixed-language static documents are not publishable.
Runtime translation remains only for content inserted dynamically after a localized document has loaded.
evidence: user production screenshots showing English selected while Dutch copy remained visible
